formacion.title: Learning fast is the skill that decides who adapts to AI.
formacion.lede: I've been a professor at Universidad EAFIT for 15 years and building software and AI for 13. I bring both crafts together in Learning Sprints for teams and live cohorts for professionals, with a method tested in the classroom and in production.

method.label: // the method
method.tryTemplate: Try the MAPA Method for free →
method.title: The MAPA Method
method.desc: Four steps to learn any skill in weeks, not months. It combines ultralearning principles, experiential learning, and AI as a tutor.

steps.title: Map
steps.text: Break the skill down and find the 20% that delivers 80% of the result.

steps.title: Apply
steps.text: Practice from day one on a real project, not in theory.

steps.title: Practice the hard parts
steps.text: Isolated drills on weak spots and active recall so it sticks.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Fast feedback, with AI as a tutor, iterating every week.

mapa.lede: Pick something you want to learn in the next 30 days. Go through the four stations, 5 minutes each, and you'll end with a concrete plan.
howto: 3 · Copy your plan or get it by email

goal.title: Your goal
goal.hint: What you want to be able to do, not what you want to "study".
goal.outcomeHint: Something another person can see or use.
goal.outcomePh: E.g. build the monthly sales report on my own
goal.whyPh: E.g. I take over reports in January

map.title: Map
map.hint: Break the skill into pieces. Then star the 3 that give you the most results.

apply.title: Apply
apply.hint: You learn by doing. Define the real project you'll build from day one.

practice.title: Practice the hard parts
practice.hint: Isolate what's hardest and practice it alone. Test yourself without your notes.

adjust.title: Adjust
adjust.hint: Without feedback you repeat mistakes. Decide who or what corrects you and when you review the plan.

fields.projectHint: Small, useful and finished in 30 days.

plan.heading: MAPA PLAN · 30 DAYS
plan.week3: {piece} + bring it all into the project
plan.week4: Finish, show the result and ask for feedback
plan.mapPrompt:
Act as an expert in {skill} and as a teacher.
My 30-day goal: {outcome}.
I have {hours} hours per week.

1. Break the skill into 10 to 15 concrete pieces (concepts, procedures and tools).
2. Mark the 3 pieces that bring me closest to my goal and explain why.
3. Tell me what I can ignore for now without hurting the result.
plan.tutorPrompt:
You are my {skill} tutor. My goal: {outcome}.
Every time I write to you, ask me 3 recall questions about {topics},
one at a time and without giving me the answer. After each answer, correct me,
tell me what reasoning mistake I made and suggest a short exercise to practice that point.

propuesta.subtitle: Take your team from theory to using AI in their real work, in weeks.
propuesta.by: Sergio Monsalve · Professor at Universidad EAFIT and AI engineer
propuesta.validity: Valid for 30 days from the date it was sent.

problem.label: // the problem
problem.title: AI is already paid for. The learning isn't happening.
problem.text: Many companies have already invested in AI tools, but teams use them little or badly. Traditional training passes on information that is forgotten within weeks: it doesn't change how people work.
problem.stat: In Chile, 66% of companies pilot AI, but only 8% manage to scale it.
problem.close: The bottleneck isn't the technology. It's how the team learns.

steps.title: Map
steps.text: We break the skill down and pick the 20% that delivers 80% of the result for your team.

steps.title: Apply
steps.text: From day one the team works on real tasks from your company, not generic examples.

steps.title: Practice the hard parts
steps.text: Short drills on the most common mistakes and active recall so learning sticks.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Weekly feedback, with AI as a tutor, and plan adjustments based on what works.

pilot.title: Pilot workshop · 90 minutes
pilot.text: To try the method with a team of 8 to 25 people before committing to the full program. Remote, live.

agenda.title: Framing
agenda.text: Why we forget what we learn in training sessions.

agenda.title: Map
agenda.text: The team maps the work task they most want to speed up with AI.

agenda.title: Apply
agenda.text: Each person solves that real task with an AI tool, guided step by step.

agenda.title: Practice the hard parts
agenda.text: A drill on the most common mistake and active recall.

agenda.title: Adjust
agenda.text: Feedback, a 7-day practice plan and wrap-up.

deliverables: A library of 5 to 10 prompts applied to their real cases
A one-page report for the team lead with observations and the recommended next step

sprint.title: Learning Sprint · 4 weeks
sprint.text: The full program for the team to adopt a new skill, including AI, in their daily work. Up to 20 people, remote.

weeks.label: Week 1
weeks.title: Diagnosis and map
weeks.text: Short interviews and a baseline survey. Team skills map and measurable goals with the lead.

weeks.label: Week 2
weeks.title: Apply live
weeks.text: Two facilitated sessions on the team's real tasks. Everyone leaves with something working.

weeks.label: Week 3
weeks.title: Real challenges
weeks.text: Weekly challenges on company cases, practice of the hard parts and async support.

weeks.label: Week 4
weeks.title: Adjust and close
weeks.text: Results demo, final survey and a plan to sustain what was learned.

deliverables: 4 recorded live sessions and their materials
The team's prompt and procedure library

carpinteria.title: CarpinterIA: learn to build your own melamine furniture
carpinteria.lede: A hands-on course in Guarne, Antioquia, Colombia, in two formats: one day to start from scratch, or 4 sessions to kick off a real project for your home. The pieces are cut to order with edge banding and you assemble them yourself.

express.label: Express course · 1 day
express.title: Your first toolbox
express.desc: For people who have never built furniture. In one day you learn to measure, drill and assemble square, and you take home a small toolbox you made yourself.
points: Pieces arrive pre-cut: no saw on day one

course.label: Full course · 4 sessions
course.title: Your own project, one part at a time
course.desc: You pick a project for your home: a closet, a nightstand, or a piece for the living room, dining room, kitchen, bedroom or bathroom. Each session is a small project that is part of the big one, and you finish the rest at home with the same technique.

sessions.title: Tools and a simple carcass
sessions.text: You safely use the drill, jigsaw and circular saw, and build a simple MDF box: the carcass of every piece of furniture.

sessions.title: Practice module and order
sessions.text: You build a module with a shelf, design your project and send its cut list with the edges that get banding.

sessions.title: Your project's first module
sessions.text: You drill with a jig, join with confirmat screws and leave your first module assembled, square and with its back on.

sessions.title: Doors, drawers and a plan
sessions.text: You fit hinges and drawer slides to that module and leave with a plan to build the remaining modules at home.

tools.label: The tools
tools.title: The AI part: error-free cut lists
tools.desc: Melamine furniture sizes depend on the board thickness and the clearances. I wrote tools that do the math so nobody has to do it by hand.

items.title: Cut-list calculator
items.text: From width, depth, height, number of drawers and door type, it generates the full cut list.

items.title: Order sheet
items.text: Turns the cut list into a printable sheet for the cutting shop, with the area of each material and the meters of edge banding for quoting.

items.title: Clearances page
items.text: Door, drawer and back-panel clearances, generated from the same numbers the calculator uses.
